questions.topic: Finding when a position returns to zero
questions.learningObjective: Find when position returns to zero
questions.stem: Position x(t)=t^2-4t. Find the later time when position is zero.
questions.explanation: Solving t^2-4t=0 gives t=0 or t=4 s; the later time is 4 s.
questions.hint: Factor and take the nonzero root.

questions.topic: Time for a stated displacement
questions.learningObjective: Compute time for a stated displacement
questions.stem: Constant speed 5 m/s. How long to cover 30 m?
questions.explanation: t = distance/speed = 30/5 = 6 s.

questions.topic: Velocity after a time under acceleration
questions.learningObjective: Compute velocity after time under acceleration
questions.stem: u=2 m/s, a=3 m/s^2. Find velocity after 4 s.
questions.hint: Add u to a times t.

questions.topic: Slope of a position-time graph
questions.learningObjective: Read slope of position-time graph
questions.stem: What does the slope of a position-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: Slope of x-t graph equals instantaneous velocity.
questions.hint: Slope of position-time graph is velocity.

questions.topic: Area under a rectangular velocity graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute area under rectangular velocity graph
questions.stem: Rectangular v-t graph: 6 m/s for 5 s. Find displacement.

questions.topic: Reading a position-time table
questions.learningObjective: Read values from a position-time table
questions.stem: Table: t=0 x=0; t=2 x=10; t=4 x=20. Position at t=2?
questions.explanation: The table lists x=10 m at t=2 s.

questions.topic: Comparing mean speeds from a table
questions.learningObjective: Compare mean speeds from a table
questions.stem: Table shows runner A: 100 m in 20 s; runner B: 80 m in 10 s. Who is faster?
questions.explanation: A speed = 5 m/s, B speed = 8 m/s, so B is faster.

questions.topic: Curvature and the sign of acceleration
questions.learningObjective: Relate curvature to sign of acceleration
questions.stem: A position-time graph curves upward (concave up). Acceleration is?
questions.explanation: Concave-up x-t graph means positive acceleration.

questions.topic: Finding when a position returns to zero
questions.learningObjective: Find when position returns to zero
questions.stem: A student solves x(t)=t^2-9=0 and reports t=-3 s only. What is wrong?

options.text: Both roots ±3 s should be considered
Only positive time is physical, but report 3 s

questions.explanation: t^2=9 gives t=±3 s; both roots exist mathematically, though only t=3 s may be physical.

questions.topic: Time for a stated displacement
questions.learningObjective: Compute time for a stated displacement
questions.stem: If speed doubles, time for same distance?
questions.explanation: t = d/v, so doubling v halves t.
questions.hint: Time is inversely proportional to speed.

questions.topic: Velocity after a time under acceleration
questions.learningObjective: Compute velocity after time under acceleration
questions.stem: A student computes v = u + a*t^2 for u=0,a=2,t=3. What is wrong?

options.text: Acceleration times time, not time squared
The formula is v = a*t^2 always

questions.explanation: v = u + a t, linear in time; t^2 belongs in displacement, not velocity.
questions.hint: Velocity grows linearly with time under constant acceleration.

questions.topic: Slope of a position-time graph
questions.learningObjective: Read slope of position-time graph
questions.stem: x-t graph: x from 0 to 10 m over 2 s. Find velocity.
questions.hint: Divide change in position by change in time.

questions.topic: Area under a rectangular velocity graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute area under rectangular velocity graph
questions.stem: If the rectangle height (velocity) doubles but width (time) stays same, displacement?
questions.explanation: Area = v*t, so doubling v doubles displacement.

questions.topic: Reading a position-time table
questions.learningObjective: Read values from a position-time table
questions.stem: Table: t=0 x=5; t=1 x=7; t=2 x=9. Position at t=0?
questions.explanation: The table lists x=5 m at t=0 s.

questions.topic: Comparing mean speeds from a table
questions.learningObjective: Compare mean speeds from a table
questions.stem: A student compares mean speeds by comparing total distances only, ignoring times. What is wrong?

options.text: Mean speed requires distance divided by time

questions.explanation: Mean speed = total distance / total time; comparing distances alone ignores differing times.
questions.hint: Speed needs both distance and time.
